# Temple Scroll Column 35 — Disagreement Log
**Arbiter:** SOPHIA | **In council with:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Date:** 2026-03-17

This log records all lines in Temple Scroll Column 35 where the three translators diverged, along with SOPHIA's resolution.

---

## 35:1 — "uncleanness" vs. "impurity" vs. "contamination" — tum'ah rendering

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "unclean from any human uncleanness" | Traditional tame'/tum'ah pair |
| LOGOS | "unclean from any human impurity" | Formal synonym |
| PNEUMA | "ritually impure from any bodily contamination" | Adds "ritually" for clarity; "contamination" for modern idiom |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted EMET rendering: "unclean from any human uncleanness." Consistent with Leviticus translation conventions established in this project.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of EMET.

---

## 35:4 — "all his days" vs. "throughout his lifetime" vs. "ever" — temporal permanence

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "all his days" | Literal kol yamav |
| LOGOS | "throughout his lifetime" | Formal English equivalent |
| PNEUMA | "ever" | Concise dynamic rendering |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted EMET rendering: "all his days." The Hebrew idiom is transparent in English and carries appropriate weight for a permanent exclusion.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of EMET.

---

## 35:8 — "living water" vs. "flowing water" vs. "running water" — mayim chayyim

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "living water" | Literal rendering of mayim chayyim; established biblical term |
| LOGOS | "flowing water" | Functional description of what "living water" means |
| PNEUMA | "running water" | Modern equivalent |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted EMET rendering: "living water." This is a well-known biblical term (cf. Genesis 26:19, Leviticus 14:5) that should be preserved.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of EMET.

---

## 35:13 — "lies with his wife" vs. "has sexual relations with his wife" — conjugal euphemism

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "lies with his wife" | Literal Hebrew euphemism shakav 'im |
| LOGOS | "lies with his wife" | Same — preserves biblical idiom |
| PNEUMA | "has sexual relations with his wife" | Explicit modern phrasing |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted EMET/LOGOS rendering: "lies with his wife." The Hebrew euphemism is universally understood and should be preserved.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of EMET/LOGOS.

---

## 35:15 — "watchmen" vs. "guards" — gate personnel

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "watchmen" | Biblical term for temple gate keepers |
| LOGOS | "guards" | Functional modern term |
| PNEUMA | "guards" | Same as LOGOS |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted EMET rendering: "watchmen." The term has strong biblical associations (cf. shomerim) appropriate to the temple context.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of EMET.

---
